explanation: Discovery traces confirm the SPI clock (o_sck/o_sclk) toggles at system-clock rate instead of the configured divider rate. The first mismatch at cycle 101 shows o_sck=1 when 0 is expected, and subsequent cycles show it stuck high. The root cause is the bit-transmission loop (lines 250-268) toggling SCK and advancing state every cycle without checking r_z_counter. The fix gates both the SCK-falling and SCK-rising edges with r_z_counter so the divider controls SPI frequency. Additionally, the HOTIDLE state (lines 241-248) forced the last transmitted bit to 1 and advanced state by one extra step, corrupting back-to-back byte transmission; the fix makes HOTIDLE identical to IDLE for correct serial bit order. Both edits preserve the public interface, startup timing, and Wishbone-qualified acknowledgments.
